title: Double Numbers
prompt: A score preview wants to show what each value would look like after a bonus multiplier. Write a function that returns a new array where every number from the input is doubled.

explanation.beginner:
Example: doubleNumbers([1,2,3]) produces [2,4,6]. Project each included record into the requested output shape, keeping the required input order.

Compare “handles an empty list”: input [[]] produces []. Explain which rule causes the difference before writing code.
explanation.junior:
Project each included record into the requested output shape, keeping the required input order.

Tempting mistake: A projection is different from filtering: returning a boolean from map gives booleans, while returning a value from filter only makes a keep decision.

The reference uses map. Trace the intermediate value after each operation; count repeated scans inside callbacks separately when estimating cost.

Regression check: preserve the contract illustrated by “handles an empty list”, then change one boundary in a new test. The solution below is one implementation; another is valid when it preserves the same behavior.
